subject.title: Agent-created crons inherit session toolsAllow at create-time; patch toolsAllow:null is a silent no-op; claude-cli backend then refuses the job

question: How should OpenClaw handle agent-created CLI-backed cron jobs that inherit or retain `toolsAllow` when the CLI backend cannot enforce that runtime policy?
rationale: The remaining fix must choose a security boundary: reject or explain restricted clears, narrowly repair inherited defaults, or relax runtime behavior, and those choices have different compatibility and tool-access consequences.

options.title: Reject or Explain Restricted Clears
options.body: Keep explicit restrictions fail-closed, return a clear agent-facing error for blocked null clears, and provide a narrow operator repair for provably inherited defaults.

options.title: Allow Narrow Default-Cap Clearing
options.body: Permit the agent tool to clear only default-stamped inherited caps while preserving explicit restrictions and proving the distinction with tests.

options.title: Relax CLI Runtime Handling
options.body: Warn and ignore selected inherited caps at runtime on CLI-backed jobs, accepting that those restrictions are not enforced by the backend.

recommendation.title: Reject or Explain Restricted Clears
recommendation.body: Keep explicit restrictions fail-closed, return a clear agent-facing error for blocked null clears, and provide a narrow operator repair for provably inherited defaults.
